questions.stem: Although the pay was good, she was ______ to leave her hometown and move abroad.
questions.explain: reluctant 指不情願、勉強。前半句 Although the pay was good 表讓步，後半須為負面態度。eager（渴望）、grateful（感激）、curious（好奇）皆與讓步語氣不合。

questions.stem: His apology sounded ______; you could tell he really regretted what he had said.
questions.explain: genuine 指真誠、發自內心。後半句 really regretted 是線索。artificial（虛假）語義相反；formal（正式）、brief（簡短）與「後悔」無關。

questions.stem: Rainfall here is ______ in summer, so farmers rarely worry about water.
questions.explain: abundant 指充足、豐沛。後句 rarely worry about water 反推雨量多。scarce（稀少）語義相反，是最強誘答。

questions.stem: His directions were so ______ that we got lost twice before finding the place.
questions.explain: vague 指含糊不清。so...that 句型的結果 got lost 指向指路不清楚。precise（精確）語義相反。

questions.stem: After breaking down three times, the old car could no longer be considered ______.
questions.explain: reliable 指可靠、值得信賴。break down（拋錨）三次直接對應「不再可靠」。其餘三字與「拋錨」無邏輯關聯。

questions.stem: Despite winning the award, he remained ______ and gave the credit to his team.
questions.explain: modest 指謙虛。gave the credit to his team（把功勞歸於團隊）是關鍵線索。arrogant（傲慢）語義相反；generous 指慷慨（多用於財物分享），此處歸功於人用 modest 才精確。

questions.stem: With enough sunlight and water, these plants will ______ even in poor soil.
questions.explain: thrive 指茁壯生長。even in poor soil（即使土壤貧瘠）表轉折，須為正面結果。wither（枯萎）、decay（腐爛）方向相反。

questions.stem: Ever since the accident, he has been extremely ______ when crossing the street.
questions.explain: cautious 指謹慎小心。Ever since the accident 表事故留下的影響。careless（粗心）語義相反；注意 cautious 與 careless 字形相近但意思相反。

questions.stem: A hot bath may help ______ the pain in your back after a long day.
questions.explain: relieve 指減輕、緩解（疼痛、壓力）。help + 原形動詞，熱水澡的作用是減輕而非加劇。⚠ relieve（緩解）與 relief（名詞）詞性要分清。

questions.stem: It took the exchange student several months to ______ to the local climate and food.
questions.explain: adapt to 指適應（新環境）。several months 暗示調適過程。refer to（提及）、object to（反對）、belong to（屬於）雖同接 to，語義均不合。

questions.stem: Getting enough sleep before an exam is ______ to keeping your mind clear.
questions.explain: crucial 指至關重要。be crucial to + N/V-ing 為固定用法。optional（可有可無）與語境相反，是最常見誤選。

questions.stem: He failed the driving test three times, but ______ he passed and got his license.
questions.explain: eventually 指最終、終於。but 表轉折，前面三次失敗、後面通過，須用表「最後」的副詞。rarely（很少）、hardly／barely（幾乎不）皆為否定副詞，會使句意矛盾。

questions.stem: The smell of fresh bread ______ her to buy a whole loaf though she had just eaten.
questions.explain: tempt sb. to V 指引誘某人做某事。though she had just eaten 顯示非必要的購買，屬受誘惑。forced（強迫）語氣過強；warned（警告）、reminded（提醒）語義不合。

questions.stem: Her ______ concern for the elderly neighbor moved everyone in the building.
questions.explain: sincere 指誠摯的。moved everyone（感動眾人）須由真誠而來。四個選項皆以 s 開頭且形近，屬字形誘答，須逐一代入語義判斷。

questions.stem: The whole town ______ over the loss of the young firefighter.
questions.explain: grieve over 指為……哀傷、哀悼。the loss of（喪生）為線索。rejoice（歡欣）語義相反。⚠ 同場景常見字：condolences（弔唁）、mourn（哀悼）。

questions.stem: ______ all the answers, the student handed in the exam paper.
questions.explain: 分詞構句表先後順序時用完成式 Having + p.p.：先檢查完文件，才開始辦理。主詞 the clerk 是主動檢查的人，故用主動形。

questions.stem: The passenger ______ luggage was damaged has filed a claim.
questions.explain: 空格後為名詞 parcel，且語意為「那位顧客的包裹」，須用所有格關係代名詞 whose。判斷動作只有一步：關係詞後面直接接名詞，就是 whose。

questions.point: 假設語氣：與過去事實相反
questions.stem: If the driver had taken the earlier train, he ______ on time.
questions.explain: 與過去事實相反的假設：If 子句用 had + p.p.，主句用 would/could/might have + p.p.。本題 if 子句已給 had written，主句須為 would have arrived。⚠ 對照與現在事實相反：If 子句過去式，主句 would + 原形。

questions.stem: Not until the following morning ______ that the address was incomplete.
questions.explain: 否定副詞片語 Not until 置於句首時，主句須倒裝為「助動詞＋主詞＋原形動詞」。主句時態為過去，故用 did we notice。

questions.stem: Reviewing code with an AI tool is ______ more efficient than doing it alone.
questions.explain: 比較級前的加強語只能用 much / far / even / still / a lot / a great deal，不能用 very / too / so。本題 more efficient 為比較級，故選 far。⚠ very 只修飾原級（very efficient），修飾比較級一律錯。

questions.point: 動名詞與不定詞之語意差別
questions.stem: On his way to the station, he stopped ______ a cup of coffee.
questions.explain: stop to V 表「停下來去做某事」，stop V-ing 表「停止正在做的事」。句意為途中停下來買咖啡，故用 to buy。同型還有 remember/forget/regret + to V 與 V-ing。

questions.stem: This café is always crowded on Mondays. I wish there ______ more tables available.
questions.explain: wish 表與現在事實相反的願望時，後接過去式，be 動詞一律用 were。⚠ 本考點 8/21、8/23、8/24 連續三次答錯（模考0821-19、模考0823-25 及改寫題）。判斷動作：看到 wish 就先問「這是不是與現在事實相反」，是就把動詞往過去推一格。

questions.stem: The developer explained ______ had caused the app to crash.
questions.explain: 空格後 had caused 缺主詞，須用兼作主詞的 what（＝the thing that）。that 引導名詞子句時後面須為完整句；whether 表「是否」，語意不合。判斷動作：先看子句缺不缺成分——缺主詞或受詞就用 what。

questions.stem: The sorting staff ______ overtime since the beginning of the month.
questions.explain: since + 時間點須搭配完成式；動作自月初持續至今且仍在進行，用現在完成進行式 have been working。since 是本題唯一線索，看到它就排除單純現在式與未來式。

questions.stem: The luggage must be weighed again ______ the passenger has already checked in.
questions.explain: 前後兩句語意相衝突（已付郵資，仍須再秤），須用讓步連接詞 even if。as long as 表條件、so that 表目的、in case 表以防萬一。⚠ 本考點 8/24 答錯（改寫0824-英14），判斷動作只有一步：先問前後兩句是相衝突還是同方向，衝突就找讓步詞。

questions.stem: You should have the damaged box ______ before sending it out again.
questions.explain: have + 受詞 + p.p. 表「使某物被處理」，受詞 the damaged box 是被修理的對象，故用過去分詞 repaired。若受詞是人且主動做事，才用原形（have someone repair it）。

questions.point: 介系詞 by 與 until
questions.stem: Applications must be submitted ______ Friday; late forms will not be accepted.
questions.explain: by 表「在……之前完成」（動作一次完成），until 表「持續到……為止」（狀態持續）。submit 是一次性動作且有截止意味，故用 by。看到 deadline 就選 by，看到 wait、stay、remain 才選 until。

questions.point: not only 置句首之倒裝
questions.stem: Not only ______ the service faster, but it also costs less.
questions.explain: Not only 置於句首時前半句須倒裝。主要動詞為 be 動詞時，直接把 be 動詞提到主詞前：Not only is the service faster。若為一般動詞才用 does/did 助動詞倒裝。

questions.stem: You may collect the item at any branch, ______ you bring a valid ID.
questions.explain: provided that ＝ if，引導條件子句，後接完整句。in spite of、regardless of、owing to 均為介系詞片語，後面只能接名詞，先用詞性即可刪去三個。

questions.point: 主詞動詞一致：the number of（回收）
questions.stem: The number of users who deleted the app ______ fallen below fifty for the first time.
questions.explain: the number of + 複數名詞視為單數（數目本身），動詞用單數；a number of + 複數名詞才視為複數。⚠ 本考點 8/7、8/23 兩度出現（模考0807-38、模考0823-16），8/21 仿真卷 C 亦考過同一組，本次換情境再測。判斷動作：先找真主詞——這裡是 The number，不是 items。

questions.point: 克漏字一：第31格（關係副詞 where）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（一）】請依下文回答第 31～35 題。

Free translation apps have changed the way people travel. A tourist can now stand in a market __31__ no one speaks her language and still buy what she needs. The app produces a sentence, __32__ is usually good enough to be understood. Language schools report a drop in enrolment. __33__ this trend, some teachers are surprisingly calm about it, __34__ the students who remain tend to want something the app cannot give: the ability to hold a conversation, to catch a joke, to sound like themselves. Demand may recover in a different form, they say, __35__ that distinction becomes clearer to the public.

第 31 格：
questions.explain: 空格後 two old trade routes once met 為完整句且先行詞 the point 表地點，須用關係副詞 where。判斷動作：先看關係詞後面缺不缺成分——完整句就用關係副詞，缺主詞或受詞才用關係代名詞。

questions.point: 克漏字一：第32格（非限定 which）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（一）】請依上文回答。

第 32 格：
questions.explain: 空格前有逗號為非限定用法，that 不可用於非限定子句；先行詞為物（a special postmark），故用 which。what 不接先行詞、who 用於人。

questions.point: 克漏字一：第33格（Despite 讓步）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（一）】請依上文回答。

第 33 格：
questions.explain: 空格後為名詞片語 the extra work，須用介系詞；後半句 he welcomes the change 與「額外工作」語意相反，故用表讓步的 Despite。Because of 與 Thanks to 表原因，方向相反。

questions.point: 克漏字一：第34格（as 表原因）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（一）】請依上文回答。

第 34 格：
questions.explain: 「商家同蒙其利」與「許多遊客留下來吃午餐」為結果與原因的關係，空格後為原因，須用 as（＝because）。so 引導的是結果，前後順序正好相反。

questions.point: 克漏字一：第35格（if 條件）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（一）】請依上文回答。

第 35 格：
questions.explain: 語意為「如果這股興趣延續到本季之後」，屬條件而非讓步或否定條件。unless 意為「除非不」，代入後語意相反；whether 引導名詞子句，此處為副詞子句。

questions.point: 克漏字二：第36格（現在完成式）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（二）】請依下文回答第 36～40 題。

Handwriting is disappearing from classrooms, and laptops are part of the reason. For decades note-taking tools __36__ unable to keep up with speech, so students who wrote by hand had to summarise as they listened. Newer devices can now capture every word, __37__ the ones spoken too fast to follow. The result is a fuller record, but also a shallower memory. Some teachers now ask students to write summaries by hand __38__ force themselves to select what matters. Researchers argue that typing captures more, __39__ handwriting captures better. What is lost when a lecture __40__ recorded in full may not be obvious until the exam.

第 36 格：
questions.explain: For decades 搭配過去的敘述且下一句用 were pulled aside（過去式），全段時序在過去，故用 were。若用 have been 則表示狀態延續到現在，與後文「Newer systems can now read」相矛盾。

questions.point: 克漏字二：第37格（including 介系詞）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（二）】請依上文回答。

第 37 格：
questions.explain: 空格後為名詞片語 the ones written in a hurry，須用介系詞 including（包括）。included 為過去分詞，須置於名詞之後（the ones included）；include 為動詞，該句已有主要動詞 can read。

questions.point: 克漏字二：第38格（to V 表目的）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（二）】請依上文回答。

第 38 格：
questions.explain: 「接受再訓練」的目的是「維護機器」，用不定詞 to maintain 表目的。for 後須接名詞或動名詞，so 須接完整子句（so that they can maintain），that 在此無法引導目的。

questions.point: 克漏字二：第39格（while 對比）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（二）】請依上文回答。

第 39 格：
questions.explain: 工會主張與資方主張兩相對立，空格連接的是對比關係，用 while（然而、相對地）。because 與 since 表原因，unless 表否定條件，代入後前後句的對立關係就消失了。

questions.point: 克漏字二：第40格（被動語態，回收）
questions.stem:
【克漏字（二）】請依上文回答。

第 40 格：
questions.explain: 主詞 a task 是被完成的對象，done 為過去分詞，須搭配 be 動詞構成被動；now 指現在，故用 is。⚠ 本卷「主詞是動作承受者就用被動」已在文法段考過一次（be to be scanned），此處為同一判斷動作換段落再測。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（一）】請依下文回答第 41～45 題。

When a large bank replaced its telephone help line with an automated assistant, managers expected two things: shorter waiting times and a smaller support team. The first came true within months. The second did not.

Critics had warned that customers would simply refuse to talk to a machine. That fear proved unfounded; most callers were happy to let software handle a forgotten password or a balance enquiry. What changed was the mix of calls that reached human staff. The easy questions disappeared, and what remained were disputes, fraud reports and problems the assistant had already failed to solve. Each of these took longer than an average call had taken before, and required someone senior enough to make a decision.

The bank now employs more people on its help line than it did before, though they do different work. Training has been rewritten around judgement rather than procedure, and the assistant is measured not by how many calls it ends, but by how cleanly it hands the difficult ones over.

第 41 題：What is the main point of the passage?
options: How automation changed the kind of work left for people
Why customers dislike speaking to machines
How a bank reduced the cost of its help line
Why automated assistants cannot answer questions
questions.explain: 全文主軸是「自動化沒有讓人變少，而是改變了留給人做的工作內容」——簡單問題被機器吸走，剩下的都是需要判斷的難題。(C)與事實相反（人力反而增加）；(B)第二段明白否定；(D)過度推論，文中只說有些問題助理解決不了。⚠ 主旨題要找貫穿全文的那條線，不是某一段的細節。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（一）】請依上文回答。

第 42 題：What did critics fear about the automated assistant?
options: That waiting times would become longer
That customers would refuse to talk to a machine
That staff would lose their jobs
questions.explain: 第二段首句：Critics had warned that customers would simply refuse to talk to a machine，且下一句立即說 That fear proved unfounded。(C)是管理階層原本的預期（smaller support team），不是批評者的擔憂——兩者容易混淆，回文定位才能分清是誰說的。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（一）】請依上文回答。

第 43 題：Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage?
options: The bank now employs more help-line staff than before
The assistant is cheaper to run than human staff
Calls handled by people take longer than before
questions.explain: 成本高低全文未提——文中只談等待時間、人數與通話長度，沒有比較營運成本。(A)見第一段 The first came true；(B)見第三段；(D)見第二段 took longer than an average call had taken before。⚠ NOT 題逐一回文定位，找得到出處的排除，剩下的即為答案，不可憑常識推斷「機器比較便宜」。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（一）】請依上文回答。

第 44 題：In the last paragraph, “hands the difficult ones over” means that the assistant
options: passes them to a human colleague
questions.explain: hand over 為片語動詞，指移交、交接。全句在說評量助理的標準不是結束多少通電話，而是把難題「交接」得多乾淨——承接前文人機分工的主軸。⚠ 片語動詞在閱讀題常以字義推斷形式出現，先看上下文的功能，再選最貼近的解釋。

questions.point: 閱讀一：細節（改漆紅色之原因）
questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（一）】請依上文回答。

第 45 題：Why does the help line now need more senior staff?
options: Because the remaining calls require judgement
Because the assistant often breaks down
Because training has become much shorter
Because customers call more often than before
questions.explain: 第二段末：required someone senior enough to make a decision；第三段亦言 Training has been rewritten around judgement rather than procedure。(C)方向相反，訓練是改寫而非縮短；(B)(D)文中皆未提及。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（二）】請依下文回答第 46～50 題。

Every few years a government announces that it will move a department out of the capital. The reasons given are always the same: cheaper offices, jobs for a region that needs them, and officials who will be closer to the people they serve. The reasons against are also familiar, and are usually raised by the staff who would have to move.

The record is mixed. Departments that were moved as a whole, with their senior staff, have generally worked well; those that left their leadership behind have not. In the second case the junior offices become processing centres, decisions continue to be made in the capital, and within a decade a new head office quietly reappears there. The saving turns out to be smaller than promised, because the cost of travel replaces the cost of rent.

What the successful moves share is less obvious than location. They were given a reason to exist in the new place — a nearby university, an industry the department regulates, a port. Where that link was absent, the department was simply somewhere else, and being somewhere else is not a purpose.

第 46 題：What is the author's main argument?
options: Moving departments out of the capital always fails
Relocation succeeds only when the new site gives the department a purpose
Staff objections are the main cause of failure
questions.explain: 末段點題：成功的搬遷共同點在於新地點提供了存在的理由（鄰近大學、受管制的產業、港口）。作者並未主張「一定失敗」或「不該再搬」，第二段已明言 The record is mixed。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（二）】請依上文回答。

第 47 題：According to the passage, which of the following is NOT true of relocations that left senior staff in the capital?
options: Decisions continue to be made in the capital
A new head office reappears in the capital within a decade
The department gains new regulatory powers
questions.explain: 第二段明言：junior offices 淪為 processing centres、決策仍留在首都、十年內新總部悄悄重現。取得新管制權限全文未提，故(D)為非真。⚠ 本題三個真選項全部集中在同一段，先鎖定段落再逐句刪去最省時。

questions.point: 閱讀二：細節（節省為何不如預期）
questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（二）】請依上文回答。

第 48 題：Why is the saving smaller than promised?
questions.explain: 第二段末句直接給出理由：the cost of travel replaces the cost of rent。薪資、興建與人員意願雖為常見想像，但原文未提，屬於「憑常識補上去」的典型誤答。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（二）】請依上文回答。

第 49 題：What is the author's attitude toward relocation policies?
questions.explain: 作者承認搬遷可以成功，但附上條件（新地點須有存在的理由），屬有條件的肯定。⚠ 本題型 8/14 曾錯（模考0814-50 作者立場）。判斷動作：態度題先找轉折與條件句——出現 mixed、only when、where…absent 這類字眼，答案就在「有條件」那一格，不會是極端選項。

questions.stem:
【閱讀測驗（二）】請依上文回答。

第 50 題：What does the last sentence mean?
options: Being far from the capital improves service
Departments should remain in the capital
Location is the most important factor
A new location by itself is not a reason for existing
questions.explain: being somewhere else is not a purpose——只是換個地方，並不構成存在的目的，呼應該段「須有連結」的主張。選項二、三、四都把作者的條件式主張讀成了單一立場。
